html:
SMTO-POL-0027 — A stuck action was cleaned up, and it never ran

GUID: 97b20ea2-6e26-5935-9ec0-27a840fdd54a
Slug: approval-cleanup-failed
Domain: POL · Subsystem: approval

What happened

  • An earlier SMTO fault left an action that was waiting for approval stuck before it started. SMTO checked its records, confirmed the action never ran, and marked it as failed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Task's activity and check that the action is shown as failed and not run. SMTO marks it this way only after confirming from its records that the action never started.
  2. If you still need it, ask the Agent for that action again in the same conversation. A new request is checked against your current permissions, and you'll be asked to approve it if your rules require that.
  3. Don't try to approve or restart the old, failed action. Its record is kept as proof that it never ran; a new request is the safe way to do the work.

What success looks like

  • The new request runs, or shows a new Approval needed card you can answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the Task's history; it shows that the old action never started.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Startup recovery found a queued launch-intent job left by the former approval-cleanup defect ("Wrong primary-key arity for native_jobs") with exact evidence that local preflight rejected it before dispatch, and settled it as failed_to_start with executed=false.

What this means

  • Recovery found a retained approval-cleanup defect associated with a launch intent; the current repair path requires exact evidence that local preflight rejected it before dispatch. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Recovery found a retained approval-cleanup defect associated with a launch intent; the current repair path requires exact evidence that local preflight rejected it before dispatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original rejection receipt, permission correlation and launch intent; a missing Gateway job alone is not proof of nonexecution.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the native_jobs row (error_kind approval_cleanup_failed, recovery_reason local_preflight_rejected_before_dispatch) and its single retained error receipt in the run. Request new work only through the current approval flow, and keep the original failure receipt.
  • Inspect the retained rejection and recovery record. Request new work only through the current approval flow after the old launch state is settled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact proven-unstarted launch is settled without dispatch and its original failure receipt remains retained.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
